summary.text: Grant Hauschild is the Democratic incumbent state senator for Minnesota State Senate District 3 and is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for re-election against Republican Andrea Zupancich.

A healthcare executive who previously worked in rural economic development for the U.S. Department of Agriculture, he was first elected in 2022 and is listed in the Minnesota Senate's member directory as an Assistant Majority Leader.

paragraphs.text: Grant Hauschild earned a B.A. from the University of North Dakota and an M.A. from George Washington University.

His career experience includes working in rural economic development for the U.S. Department of Agriculture, as a labor policy aide to U.S. Senator Heidi Heitkamp, and as the executive director of a healthcare foundation.

Hauschild was a Democratic candidate for the North Dakota House of Representatives, District 42, in 2016; he and incumbent Kylie Oversen lost the general election to Republicans Jake Blum and Emily O'Brien.

In 2022 he won Minnesota State Senate District 3, defeating Andrea Zupancich with 50.8 percent of the vote to her 49.1 percent, in a race without an incumbent; Ballotpedia lists Thomas Bakk as his predecessor.

In 2025-2026 Hauschild was assigned to the Education Policy Committee, the Environment and Natural Resources Policy and Legacy Finance Committee, the Labor and Industry Policy Committee, where he is vice chair, and the Senate Taxes Committee.
The Minnesota Senate's member directory lists him as an Assistant Majority Leader.

His 2026 Democratic primary was canceled, and Ballotpedia lists endorsements from AFSCME Council 5, Minnesota AFL-CIO, the National Education Association, SEIU Minnesota State Council and Education Minnesota.
